fields.features_heading: A Hiring File That Starts at the Application
fields.features_subheading: A signed PDF answers the questions once. Emergent's version checks the license and follows each inquiry after signing.
fields.feature_1:
License class and endorsements first

Asks for every license the applicant holds, with its issuing state and expiration date. Jobs that need a tank or hazmat endorsement check the license before the next screen loads.
fields.feature_2:
Ten years of driving employers

Builds the work history as one row per employer, with start and end dates. Rows older than 3 years appear only for driving jobs, and a gap of more than a month prompts a question.
fields.feature_3:
Accidents and violations as rows

Records each accident and moving violation from the past 3 years as a row with its date and place. A count above the limit you set sends the application to your safety manager.
fields.feature_4:
Inquiries tracked to day 30

Logs each MVR order and previous-employer inquiry on the day it goes out. Recruiters see how many days are left in the 30-day window and which employer still owes a reply.
fields.feature_5:
Clearinghouse consent as a status

Gives every driver a Clearinghouse status: request sent, consent granted, result in. Drivers grant consent inside FMCSA's own system, and the recruiter marks each step on the record.
fields.feature_6:
Code your carrier keeps

Exports the full codebase to your GitHub on paid plans. Host the application on company servers, or connect it by API to the dispatch and payroll tools the carrier already runs.

fields.usecase_heading: Applications for Every Kind of Fleet
fields.tab_content_1:
Fuel runs go to drivers with H and N on the license

Fuel and hazmat loads need a Class A license carrying both the H and N endorsements. Ridgeback Tank Lines asks for class and endorsements on the first screen. Applicants missing either one move to the dry-van pool, and this week 3 of 5 applicants reached Carla Ortiz, the tanker recruiter.
fields.tab_content_2:
Safety review for anyone with three or more violations

Lumen Delivery's box trucks are rated at 14,500 pounds and cross from Kansas into Missouri daily. That puts each hire under FMCSA's driver rules, though none needs a CDL. Applicants list moving violations from the past 3 years, and three or more sends the file to Priya Nair in safety before any road test.
fields.tab_content_3:
Two employer replies in and one reminder going out

Previous DOT employers have to be asked within 30 days of a driver's start date. Maple Ridge Student Transit hired Rosa Linden to drive a school bus, and the app sent inquiries to her 3 past employers on day 1. On day 12, hiring coordinator Ana Brooks sees 2 of 3 replies in and a reminder going to the last one.
fields.tab_content_4:
Couriers who apply with a phone and two photos

Courier drivers at Fenwick Couriers use their own sedans, below the 10,001-pound line where federal driver rules start. Applicants photograph the license and the insurance card, then enter the policy end date. Anyone whose insurance ends within 30 days is held until a new card arrives.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Driver Application Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a driver application form that meets 49 CFR 391.21 and gets the 30-day record checks started on time.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide which drivers the form covers
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the vehicles your drivers operate. Interstate trucks rated at 10,001 pounds or more fall under FMCSA's qualification rules, and single vehicles at 26,001 pounds or more need a CDL. Cars and light vans below those lines follow company policy.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Work through 49 CFR 391.21 line by line before adding anything of your own. The rule sets the minimum, covering identity, licenses, crashes, and past jobs. Carriers may ask for more. Company questions go after the required ones.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for the license class and each endorsement the work needs. H covers hazardous materials and N covers tank vehicles, while buses call for P or S. Checking them on the first screen keeps people out of jobs their license cannot cover.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask for each employer in the past 3 years with dates and the reason the job ended. Then ask for every employer the applicant drove a commercial vehicle for in the 7 years before that. Gaps between jobs are worth a follow-up question.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Close with a statement that every answer is true, which the applicant signs and dates. Tell applicants in writing that their work history will be used to look into their safety record with previous employers.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Within 30 days of the start date, get the driving record from each state that licensed the driver in the past 3 years. Ask previous DOT employers for safety history, and send the Clearinghouse consent request for the pre-employment full query.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Keep the file in one place
fields.howto_step_7_des: Store the application, each MVR and every employer reply on the driver's record. When an employer never answers, keep the dated requests you sent. That record shows an auditor the good-faith effort the rule asks for.

None explains which questions federal rules put on the form for a driver of a commercial motor vehicle or what has to happen once it is signed. This page lists the 49 CFR 391.21 contents in plain terms, separates CDL, non-CDL and personal-vehicle drivers, and then builds what a PDF cannot: endorsements checked against the work, a 3-year violation count, previous-employer inquiries tracked against the 30-day window, and license and insurance photos taken on a phone.

claims_to_source: Under 49 CFR 391.21, a driver of a commercial motor vehicle must complete and give the employing motor carrier an application that includes: the carrier's name and address; the applicant's name, address, date of birth and Social Security number; addresses for the previous 3 years; the date; each unexpired license with issuing state, number and expiration; driving experience and equipment type; accidents and violations (other than parking) in the previous 3 years; any license denial, revocation or suspension; employers for the previous 3 years plus 7 more years of CMV-driving employers; and a signed certification. Carriers may ask for more

Under 49 CFR 391.23, within 30 days of the employment date a carrier obtains the driver's motor vehicle record from each state where the driver held a license in the past 3 years and investigates safety performance history with DOT-regulated employers from the past 3 years

As of January 6, 2023, FMCSA-regulated employers use the Drug and Alcohol Clearinghouse for the drug and alcohol part of the previous-employer inquiry; a pre-employment query is a full query and the driver must give specific consent electronically inside the Clearinghouse
FMCSA publishes a sample driver employment application; carriers do not have to use that exact form but must have a completed and signed application
A commercial motor vehicle under 49 CFR 390.5 includes a vehicle used in interstate commerce with a GVWR or GCWR of 10,001 pounds or more
A CDL is required for Class B single vehicles rated at 26,001 pounds or more, and Class A combinations of 26,001 pounds or more towing over 10,000 pounds
CDL endorsements include H (hazardous materials), N (tank vehicle), P (passenger), S (school bus) and T (double/triple trailers)
Under 49 CFR 390.32, documents a carrier must keep under FMCSA rules may be generated and kept electronically, and a person required to sign or certify a document may use an electronic signature
